rank_math_title: 5 Day Mount Kenya Lakes Trek: Chogoria to Sirimon
rank_math_desc: 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek up the Chogoria route via Lake Ellis and Lake Michaelson to Point Lenana at sunrise. Porters, park fees and camping included.
post_content: This 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek climbs the Chogoria route past Lake Ellis and Lake Michaelson to Point Lenana at sunrise, then descends the Sirimon route to Nairobi.
overview:
This 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek climbs the Chogoria route past Lake Ellis and Lake Michaelson, camps at Simba Tarn and reaches Point Lenana (4,985 m) at sunrise on day 4, then descends the Sirimon route to Nairobi. It is a guided camping climb from Nairobi with porters and full board. Price on request; it suits fit hikers who want Mount Kenya's scenery as well as the summit.

The trek is graded Expert on the page, with walking days of 3 to 9 hours and nights in camps up to about 4,600 m. You need a sleeping bag and your own climbing gear, which are not included.

Why choose a 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek?

The Chogoria side of Mount Kenya is its most scenic approach, and this trek follows it past two glacial lakes, Vivienne Falls and the Gorges Valley before you reach the peaks. Going down by the Sirimon route means you see two sides of the mountain in five days instead of returning the way you came.

  • Scenery seekers: Lake Ellis, Lake Michaelson, Vivienne Falls and the Gorges Valley on the way up.
  • Summit goals: a sunrise climb to Point Lenana, the trekking summit of Mount Kenya.
  • Kilimanjaro training: a high-altitude trek over 4,500 m that is shorter than a Kilimanjaro climb.

What to expect on the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek

Day 1 starts with a 6:00 a.m. pickup at your Nairobi hotel and a drive to Chogoria town for an early lunch. A transfer takes you to Chogoria Gate, then a 9 km walk of about 3 hours on a forest road leads to Lake Ellis Camp (about 3,470 m). Day 2 is about 6 hours through forest glades and moorland, with views of Vivienne Falls and the Gorges Valley, to camp beside Lake Michaelson (about 4,200 m).

Day 3 is a shorter, steep 3-hour climb into the alpine zone to Simba Tarn (about 4,600 m), a cold camp below the main peaks. Day 4 starts at about 5:00 a.m. with a two-hour climb to Point Lenana for sunrise, then breakfast at Shipton Camp and a long descent to Old Moses Camp (about 3,300 m), around 9 hours in total. On day 5 you walk 9 km down to Sirimon Gate and drive back to Nairobi, arriving at about 1:00 p.m.

How fit do you need to be for Mount Kenya?

Mount Kenya at Point Lenana needs no technical climbing, but the page grades this trek Expert because of the altitude and the 9-hour summit day. You should be comfortable walking 6 hours or more on several days in a row. Train with long hill walks for six to eight weeks, and tell us about any health conditions before you book. Our Kenya packing list helps with warm layers for the cold camps.

What is included in this Mount Kenya climb?

The price includes porterage, the rescue fee, non-resident park fees, camping equipment, a professional guide, all transport and the round-trip transfer, meals as listed in the day-by-day plan, drinking water every day, all activities and accommodation in the itinerary, and all taxes and VAT.

Not included are climbing gear, a sleeping bag, bath towels, international flights, extra nights before or after the trek, travel insurance, visa fees, souvenirs and any government increase in taxes or park fees. Tips are extra, with a guideline of about USD 10 per person per day; our guide to tipping in Kenya explains how to tip a Mount Kenya crew.

faq.q: Which route does the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek follow?
faq.a: The 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek goes up the Chogoria route and down the Sirimon route. You camp at Lake Ellis, Lake Michaelson and Simba Tarn, reach Point Lenana at sunrise on day 4, and descend via Shipton Camp to Old Moses Camp before walking out to Sirimon Gate on day 5.

faq.q: How high do you climb on the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek?
faq.a: The highest point on the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek is Point Lenana at 4,985 m, the trekking summit of Mount Kenya. You sleep at about 3,470 m, 4,200 m and 4,600 m on the way up, which helps you adjust, but altitude symptoms are still possible, so walk slowly and drink plenty of water.

faq.q: How fit do I need to be for the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek?
faq.a: The 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek is graded Expert on the page. No climbing skills are needed, but you walk 3 to 9 hours a day at altitude, and summit day is about 9 hours. Regular long hill walks in the weeks before the trek are the best preparation, and tell us the ages of any younger trekkers so we can advise.

faq.q: When is the best time for the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek?
faq.a: The best time for the 5 day Mount Kenya lakes trek is in the drier months, usually January to February and July to October, when trails are firmer and sunrise views from Point Lenana are clearer. The rains around April to May and November make the forest sections muddy, so ask us before booking in those months.
